contentBody: **Which prompt is most likely to surface a specific, actionable finding?**
option.1: "Rank these five stores by return rate and tell me the size of the gap between the highest and lowest."
option.2: "What do you think of this data?"
answerExplanation: Naming the exact comparison and asking for a measurable gap is what makes a query targeted — the other three are too open-ended to produce something you can act on directly.

contentBody: **After an AI answers "Team A had the most support tickets last month," what is the best guided follow-up?**
option.1: Immediately move to an unrelated question about a different dataset
option.2: Repeat the exact same question a second time
option.3: "Which specific issue type made up most of Team A's tickets?"
option.4: Ask the AI to stop analyzing and just guess
answerExplanation: A guided follow-up builds directly on the previous answer, narrowing toward a more specific and useful finding — this is the EDA-style prompt-chaining habit from the lesson.

contentBody: **A single unusually high sales day appears once in ninety days of otherwise steady data. What is the appropriate response?**
option.1: Immediately declare it the new normal and update all future forecasts
option.2: Delete that day's data so it does not confuse the AI
option.3: Assume the AI invented the number and ignore the entire dataset
option.4: Note it as a single point worth watching, not yet a proven trend
answerExplanation: One unusual day is exactly what noise looks like — it deserves a note and a watch for repetition, not an immediate change in strategy based on a single data point.
